source: Puma et al. (2012), Third Grade Follow-up to the Head Start Impact Study: Final Report, OPRE 2012-45; rendered Exhibits 4.2 and 4.10 (printed pp. 78 and 91), with explanatory text on printed p. 83.
scope: One statistically significant-at-10%-threshold, parent-reported third-grade school-performance result for the 3-year-old cohort and its IOT counterpart. The pair is one outcome from the same randomized access study, not two studies.

rows.ittName: For children entering Head Start at age three, the third-grade promotion ITT impact was -0.02 (p = .092).
rows.ittDescription: Parents reported promotion for 94% of the Head Start group and 95% of controls; lower promotion means more grade retention. This suggestive result is one school-performance outcome, paired with its IOT counterpart rather than independent evidence.
rows.ittUnit: Regression-adjusted parent-reported probability impact on promotion to the next grade at third grade, Head Start access minus control; 3-year-old cohort; lower is less favorable.
rows.ittLocator: Exhibit 4.2, printed p. 78; explanatory text, printed p. 83.
rows.iotName: For children entering Head Start at age three, the third-grade promotion IOT impact was -0.03 (p = .092).
rows.iotDescription: Parents reported a lower promotion rate under Head Start participation on this 3-year-old-cohort measure. This treatment-on-the-treated estimate is the participation-scaled counterpart of the paired ITT result, not independent corroboration.
rows.iotUnit: Regression-adjusted parent-reported treatment-on-the-treated impact on promotion to the next grade at third grade; 3-year-old cohort; lower is less favorable.
